quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When should you leave more space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: When roads are slippery.
When it is sunny outside.
When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: When roads are slippery.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space between you and other vehicles when road conditions make it harder to stop, such as wet or icy roads.

questions.question: What happens to face shields and goggles over time?

options.text: Will likely never need to be replaced.
Will develop scratches and become brittle, requiring regular replacement.
Should be made of breakable materials so they can break away in the event of a crash.
Should not allow air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will develop scratches and become brittle, requiring regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Plastic face shields and goggles get scratches and become brittle as they age. Replace them regularly to keep your eyes protected.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
Travel at a faster speed than usual to get to your destination more quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Decrease your following distance so you can be as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Stay flexible about your lane position at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane to prevent other vehicles from sharing it?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
Coming to a complete stop before you expect to.
Popping a tire.
Taking too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause you to lose grip on the road and crash.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is following you too closely?

options.text: Speed up.
Move onto the shoulder.
Allow the other driver to pass you.
Exit the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the other driver to pass you.
questions.explanation: Let the tailgating vehicle pass you safely. Speeding up will only make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do if your front wheel locks?

options.text: Continue to hold the brake and the skid should end.
Release the front brake and not use the front brake.
Release the front brake and then quickly squeeze the front brake.
Release the front brake immediately and re-apply the front brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply the front brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the brake right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: How often should you use both brakes when slowing or stopping?

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Infrequently.
Only when riding in the city.
Every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow or stop to get the best stopping power.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How should you look while turning your motorcycle?

options.text: Increase your speed before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle from leaning.
Look through the turn to anticipate the best course of action.
Come to a complete stop before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to anticipate the best course of action.
questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn by turning your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle as needed.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.
Behind the left footrest.
Behind the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot. Lift the lever with your foot to shift to a higher gear. Press it down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrower view of the road so you can stay focused.
You will have more time to react to what other drivers do.
You can more easily follow the path of the next vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a better view of hazards. It also gives you more time to react and more room to move if needed.

questions.question: What is the danger of riding alongside a car?

options.text: It is encouraged.
You can be in the driver's blind spot.
It is only a problem when the road is wet.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route.

questions.question: What may cause the front wheel and handlebars to shake or wobble?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure.
Brakes that are not working properly.
A balanced load.
Excessive wind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Most wobbling is caused by improper loading, unsuitable add-ons, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake?

options.text: It is too dangerous for inexperienced riders.
Use it by itself.
Use it to occasionally help the rear brake.
Use it together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use it together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does it mean when a rider extends their left arm straight out to the left?

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals to show turns or stops instead of turn signals. A left arm extended straight out to the left means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes left.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. Tire problems are usually noticed by how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors while riding?

options.text: Never
Once in a while
Frequently
More often than you look ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to know what is happening behind you and spot hazards early.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn the location of all controls before you ride.

questions.question: What happens if you shift into a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may go off.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear too fast can cause your motorcycle to jerk and the rear tire to skid. This can make you lose control. Always slow down before shifting into a lower gear.

questions.question: At a blind intersection with a stop sign, what should riders do?

options.text: Stop at the stop sign and proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Go through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop sign. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: Why should you use mirrors when stopped at an intersection?

options.text: To see if parked cars are entering traffic.
To look for vehicles changing lanes.
To watch for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
To see if someone is planning to turn behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To watch for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to check for cars coming from behind. The drivers may not see you in time, and you may need to react quickly.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, what is best?

options.text: Let one rider finish passing before the next rider starts.
Let several riders pass at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to signal no more motorcycles are coming.
Pass in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let one rider finish passing before the next rider starts.
questions.explanation: Pass one at a time. Each rider should finish their pass and get back in formation before the next rider begins to pass.

questions.question: When adjusting mirrors, what should you focus on?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
Your arms.
The road in front of your motorcycle.
The side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust mirrors to see the lane behind you and the lane next to you. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at night.
They are caused by bald tires.
They happen at speeds over 55 mph.
They involve new riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve new riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience. Most crashes happen in daylight when riders are traveling at low speeds.
